newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds settle modestly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds settle modestly lower.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities traded slightly lower on Monday, as market participants witnessed little activity amid a dearth of economic data.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 2/32 at 100-21/32 bid, yielding 102 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was off 1/32 at 100-16/32 bid, and Freddie Mac issues slipped 3/32 at 100-20/32 bid.
It appeared there was light buying in 7.5 percent pass-through paper earlier, one Ginnie trader said.

"It may have been for (Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduit) REMIC securities," he said. It is common for mortgage agencies, such as Fannie Mae, to buy mortgage-backed certificates for newly issued REMIC collateral.
Salomon Brothers recommended a modest underweight in mortgages versus Treasuries, according to its bond market report released on Monday.

Among mortgage-backed securities, the primary dealership said that to-be-announced (TBA) pass-throughs, conventional 7.5 percent issues "appear cheap to a combination of 7.0 percent and 8.0 percent paper."
Market players will receive consumer confidence data on Tuesday at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. Economists in a Reuters poll forecast confidence slipped to 126.3 in June versus 127.1 the previous month.
The Treasury is set to auction $15.5 billion in two-year notes and $11.5 billion of five-year notes on Tuesday and Wednesday, respectively.
In Treasury trading, the five-year Treasury note was off 2/32 to yield 6.29 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was down 4/32, yielding 6.40 percent.
